label: TP
reason: Both alerts represent real vulnerabilities. Alert 1 (java/xss) is TP because the user-provided param flows directly into the filter string used in ctx.search(), which is then logged via response.getWriter().println() with ESAPI encoding applied only to attribute values extracted later, not the filter itself. The filter containing param is unsanitized and reflected. Alert 2 (java/ldap-injection) is TP because param is concatenated directly into the LDAP filter string without escaping, allowing injection attacks. Both sinks involve direct concatenation of user input into strings that affect system behavior (search execution and logging).

evidence.note: User input param flows unsanitized into LDAP filter (L59) and is logged in response (L85)
